timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Do I really need a WAF if my app has input validation?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Input validation is great. A WAF catches what slips through. Defense in depth, Peter.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What's the difference between Application Gateway WAF and Front Door WAF?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Application Gateway is regional. Front Door is global. Both run the same WAF engine and rule sets.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What do the OWASP rules actually block?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, remote code execution. The OWASP Core Rule Set covers the classics.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Detection or prevention mode — which should I use?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Start with detection to avoid breaking legitimate traffic. Then switch to prevention once you've tuned your rules.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Can attackers get around a WAF?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Sure. Unicode tricks, encoding bypasses, slow-rate attacks. That's why you need custom rules and regular updates.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: That's cybersecurity in a nutshell. The WAF gives you the high ground.
